metadata.title: Optimal class size and learning outcomes in Morocco: A normative-causal approach using PISA 2022 data

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 microdata for Morocco, restricted to 150 public lower secondary schools and 5962 sampled 15-year-olds. Because PISA employs a two-stage stratified design with unequal selection probabilities, the authors apply the final student sampling weight W_FSTUWT throughout to produce population-representative estimates. For variance estimation, they propagate measurement uncertainty from the 10 PISA plausible values using Rubin’s (1987) combining rules, and they explicitly note that they use the primary sampling weight rather than full BRR/Fay replicate-weight integration for computational feasibility in their non-standard optimization and fuzzy RDD procedures. Replicate weights (W_FSTURWT1–80) are described as available for standard PISA analyses, but the paper’s custom workflow relies on W_FSTUWT plus Rubin pooling rather than BRR/Fay replicate variance decomposition.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The paper does not describe a missing-data strategy for student background covariates or any imputation/deletion rule. This is a reporting gap because PISA secondary analyses typically involve non-trivial item nonresponse and missingness in questionnaire variables used for ESCS and school composition controls; without documentation, it is unclear whether missing covariates were excluded, imputed, or otherwise handled. The authors do, however, fully document plausible-value handling (Rubin’s rules) and trimming/normalization steps for the PV-based outcomes.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2022 Morocco microdata and restricted the analytic sample to public lower secondary schools only (150 schools). The study uses the complete available public-school sample in Morocco (no further selection beyond excluding private schools) and applies PISA data quality filters; students are the sampled 15-year-olds within each selected school (clustered within schools).

main_findings.target_variable: Optimal class size for mathematics achievement (PISA PV-based)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Global optimum (balanced scenario): 23.4 students (95% CI: [23.35, 23.36]); mathematics domain optimum: 24.3 students (SE < 0.02). Cost increase: +49.3%; gain: +25.1 PISA points; ROI: 29.1 (Good).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Morocco data for public lower secondary students, the study leveraged student socioeconomic status (ESCS), school-average ESCS, and public-school context to estimate a spline-based pedagogical performance function and an economic cost function, finding a mathematics-specific optimal class size of 24.3 students within a global optimum of 23.4. This indicates that Morocco’s class-size policy should target roughly 23–24 students (with domain-consistent optima) to balance learning gains against budget feasibility, rather than pursuing further reductions beyond the identified corridor.

main_findings.target_variable: Causal effect of class-size thresholds on mathematics (simulated fuzzy RDD LATE, normalized 0–1)
main_findings.performance_metrics: FRDD thresholds: at 23 students, LATE = +2.79 SD (p = 0.077, N = 696); at 24 students, LATE = +1.22 SD (p < 0.001, N = 662); at 25 students, LATE = +1.09 SD (p < 0.001, N = 662); at 26 students, LATE = +0.81 SD (p < 0.001, N = 662). Beyond 30 students, multi-criteria LATE = −0.10 SD (p < 0.001) and economic LATE = −0.22 (p < 0.001) are reported for composite outcomes.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Morocco the study leveraged student socioeconomic status (ESCS), school-average ESCS, and gender as covariates in a simulated fuzzy regression discontinuity design to estimate local average treatment effects on mathematics, finding positive and statistically significant discontinuities in the 23–26 student corridor and deterioration beyond 30 students for composite indices. This indicates that implementing class-size reductions toward 23–26 students is likely to yield causal learning benefits, while pushing classes above 30 risks measurable performance declines.

main_findings.target_variable: Optimal class size for science achievement (PISA PV-based)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Science domain optimum: 23.2 students (SE < 0.02). Global optimum: 23.4 students (95% CI: [23.35, 23.36]). Cost increase: +49.3%; gain: +25.1 PISA points; ROI: 29.1 (Good).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Morocco data for public lower secondary students, the study leveraged student socioeconomic status (ESCS), school-average ESCS, and public-school context to estimate science achievement as a function of class size and context, finding a science-specific optimum of 23.2 students that aligns with the global optimum of 23.4. This indicates that a single national target around 23–24 students is likely to be effective across core STEM-related domains, supporting equity-oriented implementation without complex differentiation by subject.

main_findings.target_variable: Optimal class size for reading achievement (PISA PV-based)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Reading domain optimum: 22.2 students (SE < 0.02). Global optimum: 23.4 students (95% CI: [23.35, 23.36]). Cost increase: +49.3%; gain: +25.1 PISA points; ROI: 29.1 (Good).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Morocco data for public lower secondary students, the study leveraged student socioeconomic status (ESCS), school-average ESCS, and public-school context to estimate reading achievement as a function of class size and socioeconomic composition, finding a reading-specific optimum of 22.2 students within the global optimum of 23.4. This indicates that Morocco’s class-size reduction strategy should prioritize moving into the 23–24 corridor (which still covers the reading optimum) to improve the weakest domain while maintaining fiscal and operational realism.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2022 microdata for Morocco, restricted to 150 public lower secondary schools and 5962 sampled 15-year-olds. It combines a normative multi-criteria optimization model (pedagogical performance from PV-based spline regressions with ESCS controls plus an economic cost function calibrated to Moroccan budget realities) with a simulated fuzzy regression discontinuity design (FRDD) for causal validation. Plausible values are handled using Rubin’s (1987) rules, and the analysis applies the student sampling weight W_FSTUWT throughout. The optimization identifies a global optimum class size of 23.4 students (95% CI: [23.35, 23.36]) with domain optima of 22.2 (reading) to 24.3 (mathematics), requiring a +49.3% per-student cost increase and yielding +25.1 PISA points (ROI = 29.1, “Good”). FRDD results show a “high-performance corridor” at 23–26 students with positive LATEs and significant deterioration beyond 30 for composite indices. Limitations include the simulated nature of the FRDD treatment assignment (instrument strength is only moderate) and missing-data handling is not reported.
